title: The Week’s 10 Biggest Funding Rounds: AI And Energy Top A Busy Lineup Of Large Rounds

payload.text: Want to keep track of the largest startup funding deals in 2026 with our curated list of $100 million-plus venture deals to U.S.-based companies? Check out T he Crunchbase Megadeals Board . This is a weekly feature that runs down the week’s Top 10 announced funding rounds in the U.S. Check out last week’s biggest funding deal roundup here . As the AI startup boom progresses, investors appear to be leaving few niches unfunded. That was apparent in this week’s lineup of large funding rounds, which featured AI infrastructure providers, a foundational model developer, a content protection platform for the AI age, and other AI-focused startups among the top investment recipients. The biggest investment, $2 billion, went to Axiom Solutions International , a spinout focused on cloud and power infrastructure that is hoping to benefit from the AI buildout. Other large rounds went to TypeSafe AI , developer of a fast-growing new model, and Oratomic , a quantum computing startup. 1. Axiom Solutions International , $2B, cloud and power infrastructure: Axiom Solutions International, a private cloud and power infrastructure company spun out of manufacturing services provider Flex , secured $2 billion in new financing. General Catalyst and Koch Equity provided the strategic investment by purchasing shares of Austin-based Axiom from Flex at an initial enterprise value of $37.5 billion. Flex says it plans to separate Axiom into an independent publicly traded company early next year. 2. TypeSafe AI , $870M, foundational AI: TypeSafe AI, developer of Jev, a recently launched AI model with a large and growing early following, raised $870 million in new funding with Andreessen Horowitz as the largest investor, according to a Bloomberg report . Sequoia Capital also participated in the round, which reportedly set a $7.5 billion valuation for San Francisco-based TypeSafe. 3. Oratomic , $475M, quantum computing: Pasadena, California-based Oratomic, a startup working on fault-tolerant quantum computers, raised $475 million in fresh funding led by Arch Venture Partners , Spark Capital , Khosla Ventures , Index Ventures , General Catalyst and Bezos Expeditions . The company previously raised $300 million in a July financing. 4. SignSplit , $400M, data and content protection: SignSplit, a provider of tools for protecting, licensing and contributing real-world human data and other forms of human contribution, emerged from stealth with $400 million in seed funding. W Group backed the round, setting a $1 billion valuation for the New York-based company, which was founded in 2024. 5. (tied) Vinci , $250M, AI for engineering: Vinci, developer of an AI computational platform for hardware engineers to design products, closed on $250 million in Series B funding at a $1.5 billion valuation. Advent , Temasek and Xora led the round for the Palo Alto, California-based company. 5. (tied) Atomic Machines , $250M, micro-manufacturing: Emeryville, California-based Atomic Machines, a startup working on AI-native digital manufacturing systems to build micro-machines directly from code, emerged from stealth and said it has raised $250 million to date from a long list of investors. 7. Voltus , $225M, energy distribution: Voltus, provider of a distributed energy platform aimed at bolstering grid flexibility, picked up $225 million in Series D funding. Generation Investment Management , Activate Capital and Vitol led the financing for the San Francisco-based startup. 8. (tied) Type One Energy , $200M, fusion: Knoxville, Tennessee-based Type One Energy, a developer of fusion energy technology, secured $200 million in Series B financing led by Breakthrough Energy Ventures and Clutterbuck Capital . 8. (tied) Ledgebrook , $200M, insurance: Ledgebrook, an AI-powered specialty insurance platform, closed on $200 million in equity financing co-led by Allianz X and Rockefeller Capital Management . The round brings total funding to date for Boston-based Ledgebrook to around $315 million, per Crunchbase data . 8. (tied) Arena , $200M, AI evaluation: Arena, provider of a platform for evaluating AI models, pulled in $200 million in Series B funding and said it has exceeded a $100 million annual revenue run rate. Lightspeed Venture Partners and Khosla Ventures led the round, which set a $3.1 billion valuation for the company. Methodology We tracked the largest announced rounds in the Crunchbase database that were raised by U.S.-based companies for the period of Oct. 3-9, 2026. Although most announced rounds are in the database, there may be a small time lag, as some rounds are reported late in the week.
